south-america-south-2009.notes: Problem E is printed as 'Electric Bill'; the catalogue has no name for E. The cover gives the span October 23rd-24th, 2009.

sources.evidence: PDF of 20 pages whose cover reads 'ACM International Collegiate Programming Contest 2009, Latin American Regional Contests, October 23rd-24th, 2009, Contest Session', followed by problems A to K.

south-america-south-2010.notes: Source 1 (dc.uba.ar/icpc) now holds a Wayback copy of the 2007 edition's page (breadcrumb 'icpc » 2007'); it belongs to south-america-south-2007, not 2010 (earlier reading tied the address to 2011). Source 4 names problems C Cocircular Points, D Digits Count and G Growing Strings, which the catalogue lacks.

sources.disagreement: The earlier reader saw the 2011 announcement under this address and tied it to south-america-south-2011; our current copy is the 2007 edition's page, so it belongs to south-america-south-2007 instead, though both readings find it is not of 2010.
sources.evidence: Our copy (Wayback, 2007-11-03) is the UBA Departamento de Computación ICPC page whose breadcrumb reads 'Inicio » Eventos » icpc » 2007' and whose menu links point to /events/icpc/2007; nothing in it concerns 2010.

south-america-south-2019.notes: Both sources are of the Latin American Regional 2019 problem set that the cover says was used in simultaneous contests in 13 countries; the QOJ page names the Latin America regional, not South America South. The cover gives only the span November 8th-9th, 2019.

sources.evidence: A 22-page PDF whose cover reads 'International Collegiate Programming Contest 2019 Latin American Regional Contests, November 8th-9th, 2019, Contest Session' and which holds problems A to M.
QOJ dashboard headed 'The 2019 ICPC Latin America Regional Contest' listing 13 problems A Algorithm Teaching to M Mountain Ranges, the same titles as the contest's problem set.

south-america-south-2021.notes: Source 6 (omegaUp ICPCMX2021) is a login-gated entry page: it names the contest and date and gives the scoring rules, but no problem titles appear anywhere in our copy; a capture of its problem list would need a logged-in session. Source 3 is the shared Latin American Regional problem set (18 countries named on the cover).

sources.evidence: A 31-page PDF whose cover reads '2021 Latin American Regional Contests, April 2, 2022, Contest Session' and which holds problems A Ancient Towers to M Most Ordered Way.
omegaUp entry page for 'Concurso Regional #ICPCMX2021' (April 2, 2022, 1:10 PM to 6:10 PM) that says 'You must login to join this contest' and shows only the rules, no problem list.

south-america-south-2023.notes: The QOJ page names the Latin America regional (shared problem set), not South America South. Its Attachments (statements and tutorials PDFs) could be captured as sources of their own.

sources.evidence: QOJ dashboard headed 'The 2023 ICPC Latin America Regional Contest' listing 13 problems A Analyzing Contracts to M Meeting Point, the same titles as the contest's problem set.
